title: TEPHRA on this laptop in 3 minutes: Agung and Sakurajima (synthetic demo data)
about: Every model step runs on Gemma served by Ollama on this computer: no API key, no quota. The case is invented data on real places (data/replay/demo-agung-20261014): real airlines on their usual routes, invented positions and products, labelled synthetic on every page. Its 10-minute window (07:05-07:15Z) starts after the last product, so every minute of the loop shows the disagreements, flights inside and minutes from the ash, drafts of every action, Bali closed with its recovery plan, and the JMA notice. Read by scripts/demo_local.py.
warm_up_why: One full 10-minute loop lets Gemma answer every question once (the estimate, each flight's plan, each draft, the recovery plan); the next 5 minutes are the second loop, which finds those kept answers instead of asking again, so the board and the Desk move at full speed while you present.

beats.do: Open the demo on Agung. Click "The sources disagree on where the ash is heading, 90° apart".
beats.see: About 110 aircraft over Java and Bali, 20-odd RFA flights in or heading into the ash, Bali's airport closed. Where the sources disagree: 4 to check, two on height (the observatory puts the ash above the official band) and two on direction (official area moves W, observatory reports S).
beats.say: Three sources, three different answers on height and direction: TEPHRA's code finds every disagreement before anyone has to.

beats.see: The amber dashed area around the pink official one, with the Plume reader's reasons and "Drafted by TEPHRA Assistant".
beats.say: The assistant weighs that evidence and may only widen the official area, never shrink it.

beats.do: Story › Show them, then RFA7601 (demo aircraft CPA140, Perth to Hong Kong at FL320).
beats.see: This flight: enters in about 20 min, drafted action "Reroute around the ash", and the suggested reroute (a few NM and minutes extra) drawn on the map. The list also has flights drafted to hold, change level and divert.
beats.say: The Flight planner picked the action; code drew the route around the ash and checked every number.

beats.see: SIGMET, VONA, JMA, Tokyo and Darwin VAAC flow in; the Coordinator hands flights to the Flight planner and Drafter, each step timed; advisories wait for you.
beats.say: That is TEPHRA Assistant at work, running entirely on Gemma on this laptop.

beats.do: Sign in as Dispatcher (PIN 2468), open the top draft and hold to approve; then open the airport plan.
beats.see: The draft, its reasons and the record line with its hash; then Bali, Lombok and Malang closed and the day's RFA flights re-planned, waiting for approval.
beats.say: A person approves every advisory, and when ash closes airports the Recovery planner re-plans the day.

beats.do: Area menu (top bar) › Kyushu. Click "A no-ash VAA was in force when another report saw ash after it".
beats.see: Sakurajima: Tokyo's last advisory says the ash has gone while JMA's eruption report and the SIGMET see ash, a CONFLICT; a Kagoshima arrival is inside the SIGMET area and more are on the way.
beats.say: Japan too: JMA's notice against Tokyo's advisory is flagged; official areas stay binding and a person decides.
